query: Equal-atomic NbMoTaW is a single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy with excellent mechanical properties at 1600 °C but very poor room-temperature ductility, while its irradiation resistance has primarily been proposed by first-principles calculations. What intervention could improve its room-temperature ductility without compromising its high-temperature mechanical performance or irradiation resistance? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the untreated NbMoTaW baseline under room-temperature, 1600 °C, and irradiation assessments, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a falsification experiment.

generation.material_initial_state: As-deposited, single-BCC-phase, columnar nanocrystalline Nb25Mo25Ta25W25 and Nb20Mo20Ta20W20Re20 (at.%) refractory high-entropy-alloy films magnetron-sputtered at room temperature onto Si(111); film thicknesses were 3.3 and 2.3 μm, respectively.
generation.intervention: The study compared equiatomic NbMoTaW with a Re-containing equiatomic NbMoTaWRe film before and after 120 keV He2+ implantation at a fluence of 1 × 10^16 ions/cm^2 and dose rate of 1 × 10^13 ions/cm^2/s for 1000 s.
generation.conditions: Films were deposited at room temperature under a base pressure of 6.0 × 10^-4 Pa and Ar pressure of approximately 5.0 × 10^-1 Pa for 2 h. Irradiation and mechanical testing were performed at room temperature. Nanoindentation used a 200 nm maximum depth, 0.05 s^-1 strain rate, continuous-stiffness mode, and 10 indents per sample. Approximately 1.7 μm-diameter micropillars with a 2:1 height/diameter ratio were compressed in situ at 1 nm/s. SRIM-2013 calculations used a 60 eV displacement threshold and full-damage F-C mode.
generation.structural_mediator: Re addition refined the grains, increased lattice distortion and excess free volume, and produced several-nanometer-wide amorphous regions at grain boundaries. After irradiation, NbMoTaW showed larger He bubbles segregated and aligned along grain boundaries, whereas bubbles and grain-boundary segregation were not clearly discernible in NbMoTaWRe.
generation.mechanism: The additional grain boundaries, lattice distortion, excess volumes, and amorphous grain-boundary regions in NbMoTaWRe provide defect-sink sites that accelerate annihilation of irradiation-induced vacancies and related damage, suppressing He-bubble growth and segregation. In NbMoTaW, grain-boundary He-bubble accumulation promotes boundary embrittlement and irradiation hardening.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to NbMoTaW, adding Re is expected to improve resistance to room-temperature He irradiation, yielding smaller and more uniformly distributed He bubbles, less irradiation-induced hardening, and less severe grain-boundary embrittlement.
generation.baseline: The comparison baseline was the Re-free Nb25Mo25Ta25W25 film under the same as-deposited and He-irradiated conditions; unirradiated specimens of each alloy also served as within-composition mechanical baselines.
generation.boundary: The reported benefit applies to these magnetron-sputtered NbMoTaW-based films irradiated at room temperature with 120 keV He2+ to 1 × 10^16 ions/cm^2; SRIM indicated that He and displacement damage were confined to an approximately 400 nm-wide region. Generalization beyond these compositions, film microstructures, and irradiation conditions was not established.

falsification_experiment.design: Under-/over-focused cross-sectional TEM was used to detect He-bubble size and grain-boundary segregation; TEM/FFT-IFFT characterized grain size, lattice distortion, and amorphous boundary bands. Nanoindentation load-displacement curves and in-situ micropillar compression measured irradiation hardening, strength, strain to stress drop, and boundary embrittlement, with XRD confirming the BCC phase and SRIM estimating He/damage profiles.
measurements: Under-/over-focused cross-sectional TEM was used to detect He-bubble size and grain-boundary segregation; TEM/FFT-IFFT characterized grain size, lattice distortion, and amorphous boundary bands. Nanoindentation load-displacement curves and in-situ micropillar compression measured irradiation hardening, strength, strain to stress drop, and boundary embrittlement, with XRD confirming the BCC phase and SRIM estimating He/damage profiles.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the predicted outcome is not observed relative to the baseline, the hypothesis is rejected.
